claims.text: The initial FeCoNiCr-based alloy is relatively chemically homogeneous after arc-melting and rapid solidification.
Minor substitution of Cr with Mn, followed by annealing at 600–700°C, induces nanoscale chemical inhomogeneity.
The resulting structural mediator is nanoscale chemical clustering and local compositional fluctuation.
Nanoscale chemical inhomogeneities create local regions with altered magnetic exchange interactions.
Nanoscale chemical inhomogeneities enhance local magnetoelastic coupling.
Altered exchange interactions and enhanced magnetoelastic coupling produce a larger magnetic entropy change under low applied fields.
Fine-scale chemical inhomogeneity preserves rapid heat exchange.
Fine-scale chemical inhomogeneity preserves low magnetic hysteresis during field cycling.
Fine-scale chemical inhomogeneity preserves overall mechanical stability.
Relative to a homogeneous FeCoNiCr-based control, the Mn-substituted and properly annealed alloy will exhibit increased magnetic entropy change at low applied fields.
Relative to the homogeneous control, the Mn-substituted and properly annealed alloy will exhibit reduced magnetic hysteresis.
Relative to the homogeneous control, the Mn-substituted and properly annealed alloy will maintain or improve mechanical robustness.
The Mn-substituted and properly annealed alloy will retain rapid heat dissipation.
The proposed behavior is limited to minor Mn additions in FeCoNiCr-based alloys processed by rapid solidification and annealing at 600–700°C.
Processing outside the stated composition and annealing boundaries may produce microstructures unfavorable for magnetocaloric performance.
